[00:10] Ethan: Great to meet you all. Today we wanted to learn about your goals and make sure the quickstart will get you to a first token quickly, and then we can talk about whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense.
[00:18] Tom: High level we want a self-serve API for devs to iterate fast. Free credits and getting a token in minutes is a big selling point. Also security is top of mind, Lena will cover that.
[00:27] Lena: Right, SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration for key management, and audit logs. We need to understand how data flows in hosted mode.
[00:34] Maya: Totally. For PLG quickstart scenario we typically offer a self-serve signup with free credits, SDKs that take you to first token in under 10 minutes. We also provide example apps and a quickstart deck — I'll share the link. (link: https://redwood.ai/quickstart-deck)
[00:48] Priya: When you say "first token in under 10 minutes" what's the realistic path? Dev signs up -> API key -> run sample call? Any friction with billing?
[00:55] Ethan: Exactly — sign up, confirm email, you get X free credits in the console, API key creation is a one-click flow. SDKs (python/node) have example code. The first token is usually <5 minutes if you have the sample prompt ready. Billing is blocked until credits are used up; there's no automatic charge.
[01:08] Jamal: Good. For production we need to consider latency. Some of our use-cases are real-time clinician assist, 100ms-ish targets per request. Can hosted meet that?
[01:17] Ethan: For short prompt lengths and streaming enabled, hosted can hit low latency—depends on model choice. For the smallest models or optimized variants we see single-digit 100s ms p95 in US regions. If you need sub-100ms consistently, Dedicated on pinned GPUs or on-prem/private may be required.
[01:30] Tom: How does caching/batching affect latency? We sometimes do repeated prompts.
[01:34] Maya: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching. For repeated prefixes caching can cut token compute dramatically. Batching increases throughput but can add latency — our routing can be tuned per-route so you can prioritize latency over cost for critical endpoints.
[01:47] Lena: On the security front: where is data stored when using hosted? Are logs retained? How does KMS work?
[01:52] Ethan: Hosted keeps customer request/response data encrypted at rest in our storage with per-customer namespaces. Keys can be customer-managed via KMS integrations in enterprise plans; for quickstart hosted we use our managed keys but we can enable CMK for Dedicated/Private. Logs and audit trails are available; retention and redaction policies can be configured for Dedicated/Private tiers.
[02:06] Lena: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO certs?
[02:09] Maya: We're SOC 2 Type II audited and have a security pack we can share — I'll attach the pdf. (note: Maya to follow up with security pack link)
[02:16] Priya: From an integration standpoint, do you provide SDKs and an OpenAPI spec? We want CI friendly flow for rotating keys and deploying functions.
[02:22] Ethan: Yes SDKs for Python/Node/Go, and a swagger/openapi endpoint. We also support token rotation APIs, RBAC roles, and SSO integrations (SAML/SCIM) for team management.
[02:31] Jamal: If we move to Dedicated, what's the commitment and how long to get a cluster up?
[02:35] Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits. Provisioning time depends on region and hardware—often a few days to a couple weeks if GPUs need capacity; we offer a burst policy and can route to compatible variants during setup. For pilots we typically start on Hosted while we provision Dedicated behind the scenes.
[02:49] Tom: Cost — are there clear unit economics? We need per-token costs and GPU-hours estimates.
[02:54] Ethan: Yes we provide token-based pricing for Hosted and a reserved pricing model for Dedicated. Also Redwood Optimize gives quantization and batching suggestions per workload to reduce cost; we can run an initial cost projection after you share a sample workload.
[03:07] Priya: For the pilot we want to run a small benchmark: 1) time-to-first-token, 2) p50/p95 latency on our prompts, 3) cost per 1k tokens. Can you provide a bench script?
[03:16] Ethan: Absolutely — I'll share a bench script that hits the SDK endpoints, measures cold start, first-token latency and steady-state. We'll also include recommended model variants and quantization settings.
[03:24] Jamal: Data residency — our customers are US-only but some partners require EU data locality. Is region pinning possible?
[03:30] Maya: Yes — you can pin region routing, and Private deployments give you full control of where data resides. Hosted has multi-region options and region-specific routing for enterprise tiers.
[03:39] Lena: About logs and audit, do you provide per-request audit IDs we can ship to our SIEM?
[03:44] Ethan: We emit trace IDs and per-request metadata; you can forward logs via our integrations or pull via API. For Dedicated/Private we support direct log streaming to your infrastructure.
[03:53] Tom: Any known limits for concurrency or kv cache size?
[03:56] Ethan: Limits are quota-driven and tunable. For Dedicated we can allocate larger caches; for Hosted there are sensible defaults and we can increase quotas for trial/pilot.
[04:05] Maya: Quick recap — for a PLG quickstart you can get devs up in minutes with free credits, sample app and SDKs. For production we can evaluate Dedicated if latency/cost/security requirements push you that way.
[04:14] Priya: Sounds good. What's the expected timeline to run the pilot?
[04:17] Jamal: Ideally two weeks to validate latency/cost then decide on Dedicated provisioning.
[04:20] Maya: That aligns — we'll send the quickstart materials today, Ethan will share bench scripts and we'll provision trial credits.
[04:26] Lena: We'll send over the security checklist and a short list of compliance questions.
[04:30] Maya: Perfect. I'll follow up with the quickstart link, pricing tiers and SOC2 pack. Any other blockers?
[04:35] Jamal: Not right now. One more question: function/tool calling and streaming — are both supported in hosted?
[04:40] Ethan: Yes we support streaming responses and structured outputs with function calling patterns. The SDKs have examples; streaming is recommended for UI latency improvements.
[04:48] Tom: Do you have any reference customers in healthcare?
